module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Tu-Deng Conjecture

*References:*
* [Tu, Z., Deng, Y., *A conjecture about binary strings and its applications on constructing
  Boolean functions with optimal algebraic immunity*, Des. Codes Cryptogr. **60** (2011),
  1–14](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-010-9413-9)
* [IACR ePrint 2009/272](https://eprint.iacr.org/2009/272)

For an integer $k \ge 2$, identify the residues modulo $2^k - 1$ with the integers
$0, 1, \dots, 2^k - 2$, and let $w(a)$ denote the binary weight of $a$ (the number of ones in
its binary expansion). The Tu-Deng conjecture states that for every residue $t \ne 0$,

$$\#\{(a, b) : a + b \equiv t \pmod{2^k - 1},\ w(a) + w(b) \le k - 1\} \le 2^{k-1}.$$

Tu and Deng showed that this combinatorial statement implies that their constructions of
Boolean functions (a bent class and a balanced class) achieve optimal algebraic immunity,
which is the motivation for the conjecture. They verified the conjecture numerically for
$k \le 29$ (Remark 3.1 of the ePrint version).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace TuDengConjecture

/-- The binary weight of a natural number: the number of ones in its binary expansion. -/
def binaryWeight (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.digits 2 n).sum

/--
**The Tu-Deng conjecture.** For $k \ge 2$ and a nonzero residue $t$ modulo $2^k - 1$, there
are at most $2^{k-1}$ pairs of residues $(a, b)$ with $a + b = t$ whose binary weights
(of their representatives in $0, \dots, 2^k - 2$) sum to at most $k - 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11 94]
theorem tu_deng_conjecture (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (t : ZMod (2 ^ k - 1)) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    {p : ZMod (2 ^ k - 1) × ZMod (2 ^ k - 1) |
        p.1 + p.2 = t ∧ binaryWeight p.1.val + binaryWeight p.2.val ≤ k - 1}.ncard
      ≤ 2 ^ (k - 1) := by
  sorry

end TuDengConjecture

status_issues.source_status: Complete affirmative proofs are reported in 2026. Liu, Luo and Xie prove the conjecture in arXiv:2608.05187v2 (12 August 2026), Theorem 1.1, and report an accompanying end-to-end Lean formalization. Yuan et al. give an independent proof in IACR ePrint 2026/1687, Theorem 3.1.1.
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05187: “We give a complete proof of this conjecture.” Theorem 1.1 states the bound for every k ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ t ≤ 2^k−2, counting precisely the bounded representatives and weight condition used here. https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1687.pdf, Theorem 3.1.1, independently states the same bound for all these parameters.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and cite the 2026 proof literature, leaving the mathematical statement unchanged. Verify the reported external Lean artifact before adding a `formal_proof` attribute.

sources_consulted: Tu and Deng, IACR ePrint 2009/272, https://eprint.iacr.org/2009/272 and https://eprint.iacr.org/2009/272.pdf — Section 3, Remark 3.1, and Propositions 4.3 and 4.8.

Tu and Deng, Designs, Codes and Cryptography 60 (2011), 1–14, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-010-9413-9 — publisher abstract and bibliographic information; the accessible ePrint supplied the full text.

Liu, Luo and Xie, A Complete Proof for Tu-Deng Conjecture, arXiv:2608.05187v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05187 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.05187 — LaTeX source, Theorem 1.1, proof conclusion, and acknowledgements.

Yuan, Hu, Zhang, Zhang and Wu, Theoretical Open Problems in Symmetric Cryptography: Verifiable LLM-Guided Analysis, https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1687 and https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1687.pdf — abstract, Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1.1, and independent-proof acknowledgement.
review.notes: Both declarations are faithful. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved that binaryWeight counts the one-bits and proved an equivalence between the full Lean statement and the bounded-natural-representative formulation, without using the conjecture's sorry. I also verified that hk makes the modulus positive and the counted set finite, excluding the ZMod 0 and infinite-set ncard defaults. The smallest permitted case was proved directly, and exact counts for every admissible residue at k = 2,…,7 satisfied the bound. The final scratch file compiles without errors. The external proof artifact was not audited; the status report is based on the mathematical papers.
